card.name: Likok Pulo
card.tagline: Acehnese seated island dance for Islamic preaching
card.profile: Likok Pulo is a traditional Acehnese seated group dance from Pulo Aceh - specifically Pulo Nasi/Pulau Breuh (Beras Island) at the northern tip of Sumatra (Wikipedia; ISBI Aceh). 'Likok' means dance movement and 'Pulo' means island. It was created around 1849 by an Arab Muslim cleric (named in sources as Syech Ahmad Badroen/Badron) who was stranded on the island and used the dance for Islamic preaching (dakwah). Performed by men seated shoulder to shoulder in a line, with a leader (syekh/ceh) in the middle and two rapa'i drummers, it uses body percussion and the wooden 'boh likok' prop to keep tempo, accompanied by Acehnese verses praising God. Performances are often held at night after planting or harvest.
card.insight: Like the related Saman, Likok Pulo replaces forbidden hand-clapping with body percussion and the boh likok pipe to align with Islamic propriety, and has shifted from a dakwah medium to an educational and tourism performance (Grokipedia; ISBI Aceh).
card.image_significance: Seated Acehnese body-percussion dance. A representative image shows gilded costume, angular hand poses and a temple or court setting — Aceh, Indonesia.
